events.text_en: Đồ Liệt Cơ and the eleven who went over the wall of Hắc Phong take the empty fort of Thạch Môn Trại, which Khải Lôi's garrison left in 645, and the Pivot road has a toll the Pivot did not set.

At the pass of Đan Sơn Mạch one node of the Pivot's closing array goes slack for the time it takes four of Kỷ Vãn Tình's people to carry the wounded out. The disciple who held it, Lộc Bất Quy, is not at the muster.
A hired boatman at Lãng Đào's Ngư Ca landing asks who set the new toll on Lạc Hà's boats. He is let go, and takes his own boat down to Thủy Khẩu.
Châu Phi Vân turns Giản Vạn Lộ out of Nam Phố Đường for copying the hall's order book of 1173, the one that says 'for the reed beds', and selling the copy at Hạc Đinh Thị; he walks south to Thu Trì.
The ferryman of Thủy Khẩu carries a Lạc Hà party and its crates across by night for a triple fare; the crates carry Nam Phố's cloud, and the slip says 'for the reed beds'.
Below the last cut bridge of the Ngư Ca border the ferryman Yến Hồi Độ pulls Nhạn Trận's Ngô Bất Tán out of the river. From that day the crossing at Thủy Khẩu charges no fare.
A hunter's daughter is born in a lightning storm at the Tử Tinh mine camp, and the miners' lamps go out all at once.
The hunter Bành Liệp Hổ is killed by the tiger-kind of Phục Hổ Cương; his sworn brother carries him down to Ô Diêu.
